newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Africa needs $3.7 bln oil refining upgrade - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Africa needs $3.7 bln oil refining upgrade - analyst.

text.p: Africa will need investment totalling $3.7 billion in new oil refinery capacity to meet expected demand growth reflecting a rapidly expanding population and increasing urbanisation, a U.S.-based analyst said on Monday.
Antonio Szabo, president of consultancy Stone Bond Corp of Houston, told the AIC Africa Oil conference that required processing capacity up to 2020 included:
Szabo said Africa currently had less than four percent of world refinery capacity which was operating at 77 percent utilisation, and the world's simplest refining configuration.
As a result, the region was a net importer of gasoline and middle distillates, although it would remain a net supplier of crude to the rest of the world well into the next century.
Total African oil supply was likely to rise from 5.86 million bpd in 1995 to 6.49-7.29 million by 2000, 6.6-7.7 million by 2005 and 6.46-7.66 million by 2010, he predicted.
Political uncertainties regarding Libya's supply position were the main variable factor, he added.
